Theme

Body, health & movement

recover verb

get well after an illness

also recovery, recuperate, get well, get over (an illness), convalesce, convalescence, be on the mend, get over (grief, anger), get well again

classical

Cic. Fat. 28: ex morbō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. N.D. 2.12
M-O s.v. recover, get better, get well
Traupman 296
Traupman 63, 405

convalēscō, convalēscere, convaluī

verb, third conjugation, intransitive; ex morbō, from an illness

recover, get well

The everyday word for getting well, in Cicero and the letters; also of plants and animals that thrive (Seneca, below). Those who are recovering are convalēscentēs (Plin. NH 20.34).

Other words

  • recreor, recreārī, recreātus sum — recover, revive

    the passive of recreō, with ex · also used · classical · Cic. Red. Quir. 4: ex gravī morbō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 65, 369: ex gravī morbō recreārī, to recover from a serious illness

    To be restored, refreshed: from a serious illness, a wound, weariness.

  • valētūdinem recipere — recover one’s health

    also used · modern · Traupman 65, 369: valētūdinem bonam (suam) recipere

    Traupman’s phrase, made of classical words: to get one’s health back.

  • superō, superāre, superāvī, superātum — get over (grief, anger, a difficulty)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 321

    Traupman’s word for getting over grief or anger, not an illness: to overcome it.

  • revalēscō, revalēscere, revaluī — get well again

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 369

    Poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nē aegrī quidem quia nōn omnēs convalēscunt, idcircō ars nūlla medicīna est

    nor, because not all the sick recover, is medicine therefore no artCic. N.D. 2.12 (Lewis & Short)

  • nōn convalēscit planta quae saepe trānsfertur

    a plant that is often moved does not thriveSen. Ep. 2.3

  • An convaluit? — Paulātim convalēscit, grātia Deō.

    Has she recovered? — She’s slowly getting better, thank God.Cord. Coll. II 67

  • ē gravī morbō recreārī

    to recover from a serious illnessTraupman 369

  • convalēscere

    to get well againTraupman 405

See also I feel better, improve, health, disease.
